text:
Maya: quick signal — after flipping FP8 on the L40s canary, we see intermittent ~2-8ms tail spikes on 2048-token runs. not constant, seems correlated to certain batch shapes :thinking:
Alex: saw that too. spikes only when transformer_engine is using tiled-kernel A (the new tiling probe). when we force kernel B it goes away but perf drops overall.
Jorge: can you paste the perf trace? small logs are fine, just looking for KV cache / memcpy timing.
Maya: pasted minimal trace below — repeated pattern where a single step has big memcpy and then kernel fallback. snippet:
```
[step 1024] kernel=tiled-kernel-A time=1.1ms
[step 1025] memcpy host->gpu 4.9ms
[step 1025] kernel=scalar-fallback time=3.2ms (FP8 fallback)
[step 1026] kernel=tiled-kernel-A time=1.0ms
```
Maya: note: KV cache sizes were stable, no eviction logs.
ci-bot: perf-regression-detected: job/ci/perf/canary-l40s-fp8 (delta=+5.4ms p95) :rotating_light:
Sam: could be nondeterministic tiling handshake with the transformer-engine allocator. we saw similar with early TE patches where tile alignment caused async memcpy to block.
Alex: also saw microbatch jitter — when the batch splits across two tiles the kernel picks a different codepath. that's likely why B is stable (it avoids that codepath) but slower.
Ritesh: maybe calibration numbers cause certain layers to pick an int-path then back to fp8 at runtime? any evidence of quant-switch?
Maya: calibration logs attached (pasted):
```
calib_step 45 layer.attn q_scale=0.0123 k_scale=0.0119 chosen=FP8
calib_step 46 layer.attn q_scale=0.0121 chosen=FP8
calib_step 47 layer.attn q_scale=0.0098 chosen=INT8
```
Maya: see step 47 — a single layer flipped to INT8 mid-run. that coincides with the memcpy spike.
Jorge: aha. if runtime falls back to INT8 kernel we may trigger a different buffer layout, causing extra copies to realign KV cache. that matches the memcpy blips.
Sam: hypothesis: the runtime's kernel selector is sampling layer quant choices asynchronously and occasionally re-links the tensor descriptor. when that happens memcpy syncs and we get those ms spikes.
Alex: simple repro idea: run long-run with --force-quant FP8 for all layers to see if the spikes disappear. if they do, selector transitions are the culprit.
Maya: running that now on canary. also kicking a trace with tile-alignment logging: set TE_TILE_LOG=1 and run.
ci-bot: perf-job started: canary-3422220000-forcefp8
Maya: quick interim result: forcing FP8 removed the big spikes on 10/10 runs p95 ~ stable, but average latency slightly lower than kernel B. good sign.
Ritesh: next step: make kernel selector emit a safe-switch pause (graceful rebind) to avoid sync memcpy during live requests. maybe do the rebind on a background thread and route inflight to fallback model for a few ms.
Jorge: Also add a metric: kernel_selector.transition_count per shard + record pre/post buffer_layout id so we can correlate memcpy events to transitions.
Alex: agree. also add a sampling probe for batch shapes that triggered the tiling branch — we need to know exact batch-dim patterns.
Sam: I'll open a small PR with selector pause + layout-id telemetry. keep TE_TILE_LOG enabled on canary for 24h.
Maya: thanks — will watch. if we can prove selector transitions are root cause we can either make tiled-kernel-A tolerant to layout flips or prefer kernel B for certain batch shapes.
Ritesh: if we go with tolerant tiled kernel, ensure we add unit tests for mid-run quant type changes so it doesn't leak GPU memory.
Alex: noted. I'll coordinate with eng-ml for calibration stability — maybe tighten the hysteresis on chosen quant type.
Maya: TL;DR: nondet spikes on L40s caused by runtime quant-type transitions that trigger memcpy+fallback. repro by forcing FP8 removes spikes. next: add selector pause, telemetry, and tighten calibration hysteresis. :white_check_mark:
ci-bot: ticket created: INFR-1287 "fp8 selector transition memcpy spikes (L40s)"
